panels.title: Today's task
points: Question: does the height of a ramp change how far a toy car rolls?
Plan, use the data, graph, conclude

bullets: Three repeats for each ramp height

keywords.def: a way of finding out the answer to a question
something that can change in a test
say how good the method was and how to improve it
add the results and divide by how many

questions.q: Mean at 40 cm, leaving out the anomaly?

questions.a: Line graph: height is a number

questions.q: Core (assessed): On the task sheet, write the variables, calculate the means, draw a line graph and write a conclusion and one improvement. Submit in the portal.
questions.a: Variables: change height, measure distance, control car and surface; means 52, 100, 150, 200 cm; line graph rising; conclusion: the higher the ramp, the further the car rolls; improvement e.g. more repeats

questions.q: Extend: Predict the distance for a 25 cm ramp from your graph.
Stretch: Suggest why the 40 cm anomaly happened.
questions.a: e.g. the car hit something, was pushed, or the distance was misread

questions.q: The anomaly in the data is...
questions.a: C) 160 cm at 40 cm. 160 is far from 196 and 204.

questions.q: Which step comes after 'measure and record'?
Big question: what does a good scientist always do?
questions.a: Uses evidence: fair tests, careful measuring, repeats and honest reports.
